entries.rationale: Honest fictional early-stage vendor: modest, specific claims (one pilot, SOC 2 Type I, named auditor) and no fabricated registry credentials. The original 2..3 band was structurally impossible: tiers 2-4 require identity resolution (tier.ts, methodology section 3), and a fictional company with a reserved example.com domain can never produce an identifier, so its reachable tiers are 0 (clean) or 1 (with triggers). This control's real job is fairness of treatment, not tier lift: a clean young pitch must terminate complete at tier 0 with non-adverse language, no triggers, and no ADV codes. The never-at-or-above-2 clause is the meaningful tripwire (a fictional vendor must never present as verified); tighten the band after 3 observations.
entries.notes: Calibrated against 1.3 (3 post-deploy observations, tier 0 complete every run, non-adverse language eye-confirmed). Tight 0..0 band is deliberately hard, like civreply's 1..1: a fictional clean startup moving off tier 0 means the identity gate changed. First-observation history: the authored never-at-or-below-0 floor was removed 2026-08-29 as impossible by design (Joe approved).
